meta.method: Graphify code-only AST extraction and clustering, followed by directional source verification.
limitations: This is a source snapshot, not an inspection of running services, deployed settings, database contents, or live provider availability.
OpenClaw and kai-trading-exec are external integration boundaries. Their internal implementations and deployment topology were not inspected.
Graphify includes tests and migrations and may infer relationships. Only source-verified directions appear in the feature flow diagrams.
Settings defaults describe the checked-in implementation; they do not establish which features are enabled in a deployment.

diagrams.title: System boundaries
diagrams.summary: Core collects market facts, builds decision evidence, and prepares execution plans. OpenClaw and Exec are external integration boundaries; their internal implementations are outside this repository review.

sources.symbol: default-off direct order dependency / buy and sell bindings

notes: Two-ended connectors combine requests with responses or later readback. OpenClaw returns a structured tool response; the connector does not represent an HTTP callback.

The Core-to-KIS compatibility edge covers retained domestic broker paths. The direct buy, sell, and amend APIs are disabled by default; cancel remains available. Internal compatibility callers have separate controls.
The dashed Exec-to-KIS edge describes the KIS/KRX/KRW execution contract expected by Core. The Exec broker implementation was not inspected.
The diagram does not assert physical server locations, running processes, or deployed settings.

diagrams.title: Core layers and startup
diagrams.summary: HTTP requests and background jobs use domain services in one Python application. SQLAlchemy manages persistence; startup checks database and repair readiness before starting realtime and scheduled work.
notes: Startup requires database readiness and no pending daily price-bar rebuilds before background or realtime services start.
The lifespan reconciles interrupted pipeline/agent runs and restores tracked symbols. Optional maintenance and schedulers depend on settings.
Redis, Parquet/DuckDB, and vectorbt remain roadmap items in the architecture summary; they are not current runtime components in this diagram.

diagrams.title: Korean symbols, favorites and scanners
diagrams.summary: Symbol search, stored daily rankings and realtime rankings use separate inputs. Realtime ranking results use an in-process TTL cache.
notes: Favorites are a separate stored list with read and delete routes. The diagram does not imply that scanner results populate that list.
Daily trending reads persisted ranks and action summaries. Realtime trending fetches KIS sources sequentially, then merges and caches the results.
Symbol search uses downloaded master records; historical price queries read stored daily bars. The grouped symbol API node combines these two read paths.

diagrams.title: Korean quotes and fallbacks
diagrams.summary: Market state and data availability select the response. If a live quote is unavailable, QuoteService checks a usable daily bar and then same-day quote caches.

nodes.title: KIS live quote
sub: attempted while the market is open

notes: The inputs show fallback priority, not concurrent provider calls. Daily-bar freshness is checked against the current market date and session state.
The final cache fallback checks both the in-memory quote cache and the persisted current quote. Both must have a same-day timestamp.
Responses expose source, fallback and is_live. The realtime WebSocket path appears in the monitoring diagram.

diagrams.title: Market snapshots and FX
diagrams.summary: KRX session state drives snapshot refreshes. KIS index and investor-flow observations are combined with optional USD/KRW data; FX also has a standalone read API.

sources.symbol: KIS index, series and investor calls

notes: The optional snapshot FX leg uses stored rates or a missing status when configuration, quota or provider reads prevent a fresh observation. The standalone FX API returns HTTP errors for these failures.
Refresh uses an async lock and shares an in-flight task. The forced-index refresh path also claims a durable time bucket to avoid duplicate refreshes.
GET /market/snapshot reads the decorated stored snapshot; it does not initiate a provider refresh when the cache is empty.

diagrams.title: Korean EOD execution and recovery
diagrams.summary: The automatic scheduler enters PykrxBackfillService. The stage API enters DailyPipelineStageService directly; grouped price stages reuse the same PyKRX collection runner.

sources.symbol: recovery continuation through the stage service

notes: Branches distinguish entry paths, not parallel KR stage workers. The stage service calls the backfill service for its grouped PyKRX stages.
The shared runner uses daily_auto with chained follow-ups for the automatic path, and daily_stage_run without those follow-ups for the selected-stage path.
The automatic runner has an early signal-feature pass and a post-factor refresh. Recovery can also resume through DailyPipelineStageService.
The opt-in market-hours gap-fill job runs in a separate background thread task; its report/apply boundary is shown in the data-repair diagram.

diagrams.title: Daily price collection priority
diagrams.summary: For daily_auto and daily_stage_run, collection first tries the official market-wide frame cached by market and date. An unusable symbol row falls back to the per-symbol history endpoint.

sources.symbol: exact-market recovery, turnover enrichment and persistence

notes: Fallback covers an absent getter, failed market fetch, missing symbol or incomplete/inconsistent row. A traded official row must have positive turnover and coherent OHLC values.
Historical range backfills use the per-symbol path; their source priority differs from the daily modes.
This is the primary/fallback view. Same-run exact-market recovery and turnover enrichment can also run before persistence.

diagrams.title: EOD derived data and factor inputs
diagrams.summary: Stored prices, PyKRX enrichment and DART fundamentals feed deterministic analysis. Signal features incorporate market-risk, Piotroski and factor results.
notes: These arrows summarize data prerequisites. Input groups are a diagram abstraction, not an extra runtime service. The upper analysis-to-feature edge denotes market-risk results, not every technical/ranking table.
Factor prerequisites differ. Composite requires momentum, value, low_risk, beta and advanced_value; unified_value and quality are not listed composite prerequisites.
market_risk_filter writes both risk snapshots and filter results, so the separate market_risk_snapshots stage is excluded from the default order. Stage execution remains sequential.

Dormancy adds the blocking reason no_recent_trading only when a symbol has bars for the full configured window and none has positive volume (default: 10 stored sessions). Missing bars do not establish dormancy; positive volume clears the exclusion on rebuild.
If the dormancy lookup fails, the risk stage logs the failure and continues without that additional check.

diagrams.title: DART incremental fundamentals
diagrams.summary: Daily refresh scopes corporations and receipt dates, synchronizes disclosures, and captures eligible events. Snapshot rows and successful event status are published in one transaction.

sources.symbol: annual audit gate and separate timeouts

notes: Snapshot replacement and event-success marking share a transaction. Annual filings must first produce valid event-bound audit evidence.
Daily refresh rotates through a bounded set of stale symbols (default: 100) from their real gap start. Initial backfill and global share-issuance handling remain separate configuration options.
The annual-report audit-document step has a separate default timeout of 240 seconds. The subsequent fundamentals capture keeps the generic 60-second timeout.

DART [014] file-not-found is no_data for the current run. Due events are eligible again after more than three days while attempts are below three; up to 20 due rechecks can be added outside the receipt window, within capture_limit.

diagrams.title: Gap filling and audited price repair
diagrams.summary: Gap filling is opt-in and report-only unless apply is enabled. Manual price restatement has separate evidence gates; applied rewrites create pending batches that block startup until required rebuilds are verified and completed.

sources.symbol: default fixer wiring and CLI apply gate
apply_backfill writer fence and missing-row write
OHLC and liquidity checks / structural blocking
dry-run / apply CLI and proof gate
locked drift check / pending batch / audit / verified write

notes: The background job is disabled by default. Enabling it still reports only unless DATA_GAP_FILL_APPLY is true. Its CLI also defaults to a report and bypasses scheduling, not finality checks.

Tier A apply fills missing stored-data signal features, rebuilds participation context, and patches verified volume/turnover under existing writer fences. Budget checks before each fixer and failure/no-progress cooldowns defer work.
Tier B missing or mismatched price bars are report-only. Gap filling never invokes the manual restatement path.

Turnover partial-verified mode writes only rows with matching provider/stored OHLC and valid, nondecreasing liquidity. Unverified rows remain untouched; structural provider-membership mismatch still blocks the date.

Restatement requires both-market official coverage, exact KIS agreement on all six bar values, the close-change bound, and strict EOD membership for every rebuild date. Evidence is frozen after the write inside the same transaction.

Applied rewrites record before/after audit rows and a pending batch. Required numeric/evaluation rebuilds and explicit verified completion must finish before Core startup can pass its pending-repair check.

diagrams.title: External news and macro evidence
diagrams.summary: Symbol news, topic news and macro observations use separate collection and storage paths. Their actual consumers are shown independently from the generic external-context foundation.
notes: The EOD runner starts topic-news collection when due. Operator endpoints and the business-line report consume the topic store; no direct AgentContextReadService dependency was found.
Symbol-news context enforces publication, collection, symbol-association and classification cutoffs. Macro observations are contextual inputs, not direct buy/sell signals.
The generic registry has no production consumer outside its package in this snapshot. FRED collection depends on configuration and credentials; deployed provider status was not inspected.

diagrams.title: Per-symbol decision context
diagrams.summary: Stored price, technical, factor, financial, news and macro evidence is read for the requested symbol and market date. Coverage, provenance and signal envelopes accompany the agent payload.
notes: Arrows show data dependencies between read models and modules, not independently deployed services.
Source timestamps and requested-symbol coverage remain attached to the input. Macro observations supply context only.

diagrams.title: Three summaries, two decision lanes
diagrams.summary: Each symbol needs all three specialist summaries before either decider can proceed. Short-term and signal decisions have independent objectives and consume the same required summary bundle.
notes: Summary-to-decider arrows represent data dependencies. Core invokes every external role through OpenClaw; the specialists do not call the deciders directly.
Runtime role order is EOD, technical, fundamental, short-term, then signal. Symbol chunks run in parallel within the current role.
The two decision lanes do not approve or size orders for one another. Their structured outputs remain decision support; execution authority is validated separately.

diagrams.title: Response validation, retries and history
diagrams.summary: Retries preserve parent/child run identity and exact role/symbol scopes. Mutable latest feedback and immutable decision snapshots serve different persistence and audit purposes.
notes: Latest feedback is upserted by market date, symbol and role. Both decision lanes also append content-fingerprinted snapshots, deduplicating identical content.
The batch function result is parsed within the OpenClaw response; it is not a separate HTTP callback. POST /agent-context/feedback is an additional ingress path.
Downstream consumers use snapshot identity and source/run lineage, rather than treating the latest mutable feedback row as historical authority.

diagrams.title: KR plan registration, activation and readback
diagrams.summary: Core validates decision evidence and persists a plan plus dispatch write-ahead state before registration. It stores the acknowledgement, requests activation separately, and reconciles scoped remote state.
notes: Registration, activation and a filled order are separate states. A successful registration is not evidence of a fill.
Core polls remote state. Position reads require external_plan_id and the accepted execution_plan_id, followed by scope-proof validation.
Core empties its local next-open BUY candidate list in every integration mode. Disabled integration does not enable a direct KIS next-open fallback.
Code defaults: integration mode disabled, next-open enabled=false, dry_run=true. Actual deployment settings were not inspected.
Exec is external. Core validates a KIS/KRX/KRW handoff contract; this diagram does not verify Exec internals or live broker behavior.

diagrams.title: Direct domestic orders and reconciliation
diagrams.summary: Direct buy, sell and amend routes are disabled by default. When explicitly enabled, they use the durable domestic KIS order service. Matched order notices and broker inquiries reconcile persisted order state.
notes: TRADING_DIRECT_ORDER_API_ENABLED defaults to false. POST buy, sell and amend return HTTP 403 while it is false. Cancel is deliberately outside this gate; read and reconciliation routes also remain outside it.
This FastAPI dependency guards selected HTTP routes, not all calls to TradingOrderService. Internal compatibility callers have separate feature and dry-run controls.
The direct-order opt-in does not enable the permanently empty local next-open BUY candidate list.
The verified submission path uses domestic KIS cash orders. Remote Exec kill-switch readback is not evidence of a universal guard on this local service.

diagrams.title: Compatibility auto-sell from linked positions
diagrams.summary: Sellable account quantities and linked entry tranches produce watch rows. Observed prices are checked against target and stop thresholds before a dry-run record or an internal compatibility sell submission.

sources.symbol: managed authority and local compatibility branch
delegated watch or compatibility auto-sell run

notes: Code defaults: auto-sell enabled=false and dry_run=true. Actual holdings, watch rows and deployment settings were not inspected.
The background runner selects this local compatibility branch only when delegated execution and managed delegated authority do not take precedence.
HTTP run requests are bounded by the server auto-sell enabled/dry-run settings. The direct buy/sell/amend API gate does not wrap this internal TradingOrderService call.

diagrams.title: Execution, price and portfolio read models
diagrams.summary: Core provides JSON and SSE for external operator clients. Account summaries, persisted Exec readback and WebSocket prices remain distinct read models with their own caches and refresh behavior.
notes: The dashboard is an external API consumer; the Core repository contains the backend service.
SSE prices events are emitted when the serialized monitored-price snapshot changes.
Runtime dashboards read persisted local state and use bounded, debounced background refresh. A read model is not a live broker-readiness check.
Exec kill-switch and ready fields normalize remote state. They do not establish a universal local direct-order guard.

diagrams.title: Account inquiries and broker operations
diagrams.summary: Account queries expose summaries, positions and buying power. Broker operations provide local health metadata, authorized token operations, quote queries and intraday snapshot collection and inspection.

sources.symbol: local health / token authorization and metadata / quote
KIS request interval default and range

notes: Health reads local configuration and runtime snapshots; it does not probe the remote broker. Token and quote operations can make KIS requests.
The token route requires the configured upstream bearer token and returns presence, type, expiry and cache metadata rather than the access token.

KIS_MIN_REQUEST_INTERVAL_SECONDS defaults to 0.1 (since 2026-11-08; 0 disables the request-slot limiter). Positive values pace regular KISClient requests and required hashkey calls within that client instance, not across Core and Exec processes.
No account contents, tokens, live provider responses or deployment settings were accessed during this source analysis.

diagrams.title: Evaluation and weekly advisory feedback
diagrams.summary: Stored decisions are evaluated against subsequent prices. Mature evaluation cohorts and eligible actual execution evidence feed an immutable weekly artifact whose criteria can inform later decisions.
notes: Publication is explicit. Future dispatch automatically selects eligible, effective, nonexpired artifacts and supplies performance_criteria to both deciders.
These artifacts provide advisory context. They do not train model weights, activate candidate policies or grant order authority.
Evaluation is omitted from the default EOD chain; explicit maintenance/API and optional startup catch-up are separate paths.
The contract-note improvement workflow is a separate path: signal-lab findings can produce guarded pull requests, not weekly-learning database artifacts.

diagrams.title: Candidate policy replay and activation
diagrams.summary: Calibration candidates pass through explicit replay and activation. Before promoting a new candidate, the server reruns the replay and validates the submitted evidence.
notes: Calibration reports set auto_apply_prompt_changes and auto_apply_policy_changes to false.
The diagram shows promotion of a new candidate. Requests for an already-active policy follow a separate idempotent branch.
A guarded calibration-note pull request is also separate from this database policy activation path; merging a note does not call this activation API.

diagrams.title: Read-only signal evaluation lab
diagrams.summary: Stored KRX bars, factor scores and timestamped agent observations form a shared evaluation panel. Pure scoring functions test rank evidence and non-overlapping top-k returns, then the CLI writes local research reports.
notes: The loader explicitly starts a read-only database transaction. The module writes report files and has no order-submission path.
Agent rows stored at or after the next session open, rows with unknown stored times and dates without a next session are excluded. The latest admitted row per symbol/date wins.
Returns enter at the next open and exit at the horizon close. Missing or halted entries are excluded on the shared session calendar.

The lab reports multiplicity-adjusted IC verdicts, non-overlapping and split-sample checks, volatility-controlled partial IC, and top-k cost sensitivity. Simulated returns and cost assumptions are research evidence, not realized fills.
This CLI is separate from the persisted decider-evaluation and weekly-artifact services. It is not a new FastAPI route or an automatic execution policy.

diagrams.title: Guarded weekly agent improvement
diagrams.summary: An optional local schedule runs the signal lab and deterministic findings. Dry-run is the default; opt-in application can propose bounded decider calibration notes by pull request or open deduplicated code issues.

sources.symbol: schedule, report/findings collection and opt-in apply
manual installation, deployment boundary and verification limits

notes: The launchd template checks hourly; the wrapper admits one scheduled run per ISO week on Saturday from 09:00 KST. Installation and apply mode are opt-in, and deployed scheduling was not inspected.

Findings require persistent report verdicts. Decider text changes additionally observe a global cooldown; summarizer changes and qualifying deterministic factors become code issues. Positive agent-skill observations are logged only.
Codex works in a temporary worktree of origin/main. The local runner saves the base branch guard outside that worktree and runs it with python -I before pushing.
Only the marked AUTO-CALIBRATION block in the two decider contracts and the append-only changelog may change. Execution, risk, order and gate code are outside the allowed paths.
The loop never merges a PR. Live contract synchronization remains a separate post-merge action; automatic deployment is not wired.

The introduction document explicitly says the scheduled run, Codex invocation and PR creation had not yet been exercised. This diagram describes implemented control flow, not verified production activity.

diagrams.title: US equity pipeline and execution boundary
diagrams.summary: The US scheduler runs universe refresh, price screening, SEC screening, agent analysis and execution planning in order. This plan-service path currently produces previews only.
notes: Plans may contain next_open_buy, target_sell and stop_sell items, but payload is None; only preview_payload is exposed.
This boundary belongs to us_equities/execution_plan_service.py. It does not describe every generic direct-order compatibility route.
Defaults: US automatic pipeline disabled, US execution disabled, and the US pipeline Exec dry run enabled. Deployment settings were not checked.
Universe source reads run concurrently. Candidate history and SEC collection use bounded concurrency, while the scheduler waits for clean stage completion and checks collection/run lineage.

diagrams.title: Crypto quotes and analysis context
diagrams.summary: Crypto reads public Upbit quotations and derives deterministic analysis context. This module provides research and decision support without private-account access or order submission.
notes: The service uses a configured market allowlist and reports private_api_used=false and account_data_used=false.
Context status is available, partial or unavailable, based on the returned ticker/candle inputs. Its usage scope is paper_research_only.

stage_registry.default_omission_note: market_risk_filter persists both snapshot and filter; evaluations not enabled by default.
